### Decimal Expansions

::: {#def-decimal}
## Decimal Expansion
The infinite decimal $0.d_1d_2d_3\ldots$ with digits $d_k \in \{0,1,\ldots,9\}$ represents the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} d_n / 10^n$.
:::

::: {#thm-decimal-convergence}
Every infinite decimal converges to a real number in $[0,1]$.
:::

::: {#thm-decimal-existence}
Every $x \in [0,1)$ has a decimal expansion.
:::

### Uniqueness

::: {#thm-decimal-uniqueness}
Decimal representations are unique except for trailing $9$s: $0.d_1 d_2 \cdots d_k 999\ldots = 0.d_1 d_2 \cdots (d_k+1) 000\ldots$
:::

::: {#cor-point-nine-repeating}
$0.999\ldots = 1$.
:::

### Characterizing Rationals

::: {#thm-rationals-periodic}
$x \in \QQ$ if and only if its decimal expansion is eventually periodic.
:::

::: {#cor-irrational-nonperiodic}
## (Exercise)
$x$ is irrational if and only if its decimal expansion is not eventually periodic.
:::
